39 Which particle is not a lepton?
A
electron
B
neutrino
C
neutron
D
positron

hints: Notice the wording not a lepton, so you must test electron, neutrino, neutron and positron against the definition of a lepton.
Recall that leptons are fundamental particles with no quark content, while hadrons such as baryons are made of quarks.
Compare the quark content of the neutron with the other three particles to find which one is a three-quark baryon.
walkthrough: Recall the rule: leptons are fundamental particles that are not made of quarks, for example electrons and neutrinos, while hadrons are made of quarks.
Check the electron: it is fundamental, has lepton number $+1$, and contains no quarks, so it is a lepton.
Check the neutrino and the positron: the neutrino is a fundamental neutral lepton, and the positron is the antilepton of the electron, so both are leptons.
Check the neutron: it has quark composition $udd$, so it is made of three quarks and is classified as a baryon, which is a type of hadron.
Only the neutron is a hadron and not a lepton. This is option C.

A.explanation: The electron is a charged lepton and a fundamental particle with no quark structure.

B.explanation: The neutrino is a neutral lepton and a fundamental particle in the same family as the electron.

C.explanation: The neutron is a baryon made of three quarks, so it is a hadron and not a lepton.

D.explanation: The positron is the antiparticle of the electron and is also a lepton.
